items.title: Energy Secretary Chris Wright tells CNBC more than 17 million barrels of oil transited Hormuz on Monday
items.description: The Energy secretary spoke to CNBC's Brian Sullivan in Venezuela on Wednesday, after President Donald Trump announced a massive oil deal with Caracas.

items.title: Trump to meet with travel industry CEOs as White House touts World Cup tourism boost
items.description: Trump’s meeting with travel executives comes after a World Cup that showcased his unusually close relationship with FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

items.title: Thyme Care raises $125 million, pushing cancer care startup's valuation above $2 billion
items.description: Thyme Care has raised $125 million from investors in a deal doubling the cancer startup's valuation as it tackles critical disease treatment gaps.

items.title: Uber to cut 10% of workforce in bid to move 'simpler and faster'
items.description: Uber is cutting small teams by nearly half and allowing about 1% of its workforce to continue working remotely.

items.title: Iran says two tankers have hit Hormuz naval mines, attacks regional targets in retaliation to U.S. strikes
items.description: U.S. forces completed another wave of strikes against Iran on Tuesday stateside, hitting multiple Revolutionary Guard sites across the country.

items.title: Ford continues ramping up pickup truck production as sales fall 10.3% in August
items.description: An increase in the supply of pickup trucks comes as Ford experienced its eighth consecutive month of year-over-year U.S. new vehicle sales declines in August.

items.title: Private payrolls rose by 38,000 in August, less than expected, ADP reports
items.description: Though job creation held positive, August was the smallest gain since January and reflective of a broader slowdown in the labor market.

items.title: Berkshire CEO Abel says Alphabet a 'significant player' in AI after growing stake in Q2
items.description: Abel said Berkshire has a clear view of the impacts AI is having across its portfolio of companies, and Google's position relative to the technology is strong.

items.title: Bank of Canada mulls Trump tariff shock as it holds interest rates
items.description: The U.S.-Canada trade dispute and the descent into a retaliatory tariff blitz complicated the job for the Bank of Canada in its Wednesday decision.

items.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela operations, doubling production through $7 billion investment
items.description: Chevron's move comes amid a U.S. push to increase oil production in Venezuela.

items.title: American Airlines continues premium push with redesigned Boeing planes
items.description: American Airlines is adding its most premium seats to its largest planes, which it uses for its most popular long international flights.

items.title: New York Fed's Williams says yield surge due to strong economic prospects
items.description: The central bank policymaker in a CNBC interview did not commit on whether he thinks an interest rate hike is necessary.

items.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Wednesday
items.description: Dell might've delivered the best quarter of the year.

items.title: U.S. crude near $90 as Iran retaliates with strikes on Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain
items.description: Oil prices were volatile Wednesday, as Mideast tensions continue to escalate after the U.S. attacked Iran, while Tehran reportedly struck back at U.S. allies.

items.title: There is 'a lot more pushback' on data center construction, Berkshire CEO Greg Abel tells CNBC
items.description: The resistance to data centers is gaining steam and occurring nationwide.

items.title: Demand for riskier mortgages rises along with interest rates
items.description: Mortgage rates continue to rise, pushing some buyers to riskier, adjustable-rate loans in order to find savings. Rates are at the highest level since June 2025.

items.title: Apple shares are doing something they haven't done in 20 years. Here’s what’s happening
items.description: Apple stock hasn't been this inversely correlated to its tech peers since 2005.

items.title: Berkshire CEO Greg Abel says Japanese bond yields not a challenge for trading houses right now
items.description: In an appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box," Greg Abel said that yields in the country are still relatively low.

items.title: Zelenskyy says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine expands drone operations
items.description: Zelenskyy urged airlines to avoid Russian airspace, warning that expanding Ukrainian drone operations are making the skies increasingly unsafe.

items.title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp backs ousted Ukraine defense minister's new defense tech startup
items.description: Fedorov is launching a defense tech company backed by Palantir CEO Alex Karp, aiming to turn Ukraine’s wartime experience into new technologies.
